content:
We need propose retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999 (we can't get prices but assume buyable). Need to construct JSON route.

Target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

We can think disconnections:

1. Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. So precursor1: p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) (SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1) which is buyable (we saw true). Precursor2: sulfonyl chloride with aryl group: maybe 4-(phenylsulfonyl)chloride? Actually we need sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated amide side chain. So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride: 4-(... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride? The aryl part is phenyl with side chain /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So we could have that aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl). Could we get that via sulfonylation of the aniline with aryl sulfonyl chloride? Yes.

Thus step1: sulfonylation: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride -> target.

Now need aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor: aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) where Ar = phenyl with side chain (trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to aniline). Could be made via chlorosulfonation of that aryl (Ar-H) to give Ar-SO2Cl. So precursor: the aryl (phenyl) with side chain but without sulfonyl chloride: i.e., 4-(trans-α,β-unsaturated amide aniline) phenyl? Actually the aryl is phenyl bearing the side chain at para position? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to sulfonamide N, and that phenyl has the side chain at para? Let's parse: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So sulfonyl attached to phenyl (c2ccc...cc2) which has a para substituent: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (an anilide). So the aryl sulfonyl chloride would be: c1ccc(SO2Cl)cc1 with that side chain? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl at the position where N attaches in target. So the aryl sulfonyl chloride is the phenyl with side chain, bearing SO2Cl at position 1 (where N attaches). So we need that aryl sulfonyl chloride.

We can get it by chlorosulfonation of the aryl (the phenyl with side chain). So we need the aryl (phenyl with side chain) as precursor: 4-(trans-α,β-unsaturated amide aniline) phenyl (i.e., 4-(C=C-C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N) phenyl). SMILES: c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1 (no sulfonyl). Let's check: that is the phenyl ring with side chain. Is that commercially available? Possibly not. Could we instead make the side chain via amide formation later? Another disconnection: break the amide C=O bond to give an acid and aniline. So we could have the aryl with a carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The side chain is trans-α,β-unsaturated amide: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we could form the amide by coupling an acrylic acid derivative with an aniline.

Thus propose route:

Step 1 (final): Sulfonylation of p-toluidine with aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) to give target.

Step 2: Synthesize aryl sulfonyl chloride from aryl (phenyl with side chain) via chlorosulfonation (SO3Cl). So precursor: aryl (phenyl with side chain) (call it Ar-H). Is Ar-H commercially available? Might be not. Could we instead make it via Suzuki coupling? Another approach: start from 4-bromo phenyl with side chain, then sulfonylate after coupling.

Alternative route: Build the phenyl with side chain via Suzuki coupling of a boronic acid (aniline) with a vinyl sulfonyl chloride? Might be complex.

Given limited steps (max 3), we need simple commercially available precursors.

Maybe we can use a different disconnection: break the C=C double bond to give aldehyde and amine? Not.

Consider using a known sulfonyl chloride: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) is cheap. But our target has sulfonyl attached to phenyl with side chain, not to tolyl. So maybe we could reverse: first sulfonylate the phenyl with side chain using TsCl? No.

Maybe we can invert: first form the sulfonamide between p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-(trans-α,β-unsaturated amide aniline) phenyl. That sulfonyl chloride could be made from 4-(trans-α,β-unsaturated amide aniline) phenyl sulfonic acid (Ar-SO3H) via conversion to chloride (SO2Cl). Sulfonic acid could be made via sulfonation of the aryl (using fuming sulfuric acid). That is a single step from aryl.

Thus we need aryl (phenyl with side chain) as starting material. Could that be commercially available? Possibly 4-(2-oxo-2-phenylacetamido)styrene? Not sure.

Alternative: Use a different disconnection: break the sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and aniline with side chain (the other phenyl). But the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl with side chain, not to tolyl. So we could swap: make sulfonamide between the side-chain phenyl amine and p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, then later do a Suzuki coupling to attach the phenyl with side chain? Not.

Maybe we can propose a route using three steps where each leaf is a simple commercial chemical: p-toluidine, 4-bromobenzaldehyde, aniline, etc., using known reactions: Suzuki coupling, Wittig, amide formation, sulfonylation.

We can design synthetic sequence:

Step A: Prepare the aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) via chlorosulfonation of 4-bromo-phenyl with side chain? Actually we need side chain attached before sulfonylation.

Plan:

1. Start with 4-bromoacetophenone? Not.

Better: Build the phenyl with side chain via Heck coupling of 4-bromo aniline with acrylamide? The side chain is trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to aniline. Could be made by Heck coupling of 4-bromo aniline (or 4-bromo phenyl) with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). Acrylamide with aniline substituent is itself maybe commercially available: N-phenylacrylamide (SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1). That's the side chain without the extra phenyl? Wait the side chain is C= C C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (an aniline). That's N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Actually N attached to phenyl with NH2 at para? The SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc3ccccc3N indicates an anilide where the aniline has an NH2 substituent at para? No, c3ccccc3N is an aniline (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (anilide). So the side chain is N-phenyl-2-propenamide where the phenyl has an NH2 substituent? Actually c3ccccc3N is an aniline (phenyl with NH2). So the amide nitrogen is attached to that phenyl (i.e., N-phenyl-2-propenamide where the phenyl has an NH2 substituent). So the side chain is N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Wait the phenyl is unsubstituted except the NH2 at para? The SMILES c3ccccc3N indicates aniline (NH2 at position 1). So the amide nitrogen attaches to the phenyl at position 1 (the same carbon bearing NH2). So it's N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Actually the phenyl has NH2 at the same carbon as the amide attachment, which is not possible (two substituents on same carbon). So maybe the SMILES is ambiguous: Nc3ccccc3 is an aniline (NH2 attached to aromatic carbon). The amide nitrogen attaches to that carbon (makes N-aryl amide). So the amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl (forming anilide) and the phenyl also has an NH2 substituent at para? No, the SMILES "Nc3ccccc3" is an aniline where the N is attached to the aromatic carbon (the N is external). In "C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N", the carbonyl carbon is attached to N, which is attached to aromatic carbon (forming anilide). Then that aromatic carbon also has an N attached? Actually "c3ccccc3N" means the aromatic ring has an N attached as substituent (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (forming N-aryl amide) and the aromatic ring also has an NH2 substituent at another position (maybe para). So the side chain is N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide.

Thus we could get N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide commercially? Possibly not.

Given complexity, maybe we can propose a route with three steps using commercially available building blocks: p-toluidine, 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride, and trans-cinnamic acid? Let's think: Could we form the target by first forming sulfonamide between p-toluidine and 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (which has NH2 on the ring). Then we need to attach the trans-α,β-unsaturated amide onto that ring via amide formation with trans-cinnamic acid? Actually the sulfonyl phenyl already has an NH2 that can be acylated with trans-cinnamic acid chloride to give the side chain. So route:

Step 1: Sulfonyl chloride: 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (SMILES: Nc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1). Is this commercially available? Likely yes. Check buyable: we can test.
